title: Regional spot + fallback matrix runbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working runbook and lightweight cost model describing a pragmatic policy for mixing spot instances across regions with explicit fallback tiers. Goal: minimize spend while keeping P95 latency < 250ms for customer tier=standard and < 100ms for customer tier=enterprise, and keep token-quality regressions below 1% relative to baseline model.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: product optimize, serving runtime, SRE, solutions eng.
- Scope: policy for request routing by region + instance procurement (spot vs on-demand) and ordered fallback tiers when capacity is constrained. Not covering private (on-prem) customers.

High level idea (one paragraph):
Instead of a single global fallback policy, split routing into regional primary pools with a configurable spot mix and a 3-tier fallback ladder per region. At runtime, requests try: 1) regional spot pool (low cost), 2) regional reserved/on-demand pool (medium cost), 3) cross-region pooled capacity (higher cost + latency), 4) throttled-slo-deny or degrade to cheaper model (last resort). We encode cost/latency tradeoffs and a probabilistic capacity model (empirical p(success) for each tier by hour-of-day) into a small spreadsheet used by the autoscaler/optimizer for bump suggestions and for CSM pricing conversations.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Spot price / per-token run cost scales linearly with GPU hour price. For modeling we use representative numbers: spot GPU-hour USD: 0.45, on-demand GPU-hour USD: 1.20.
- Average tokens per request: 60. Average GPU tokens/sec throughput per GPU: 6000 tokens/sec sustained for batched regenerative workloads.
- Network cross-region latency penalty: +20ms for nearby region, +50ms for cross-continent.
- Failure modes: spot reclamation rate modeled as percent of minutes reclaimed per hour window (alpha). We use historical: alpha = 0.8% / hour for stable regions, 3% / hour for volatile regions.
- Target SLOs: see top.

Model variables (spreadsheet column names):
- region (string)
- hour_of_day (0-23)
- spot_mix_pct (0-100) -- proportion of capacity provisioned as spot in region pool
- spot_reclaim_rate_pct_per_hr (numeric)
- base_gpu_cost_spot_usd_hr
- base_gpu_cost_od_usd_hr
- tokens_per_request
- avg_seq_len (tokens)
- gpu_throughput_tokens_per_sec
- batch_effective_multiplier (1.0-4.0)
- latency_slo_ms
- cross_region_latency_overhead_ms
- fallback_order (comma-separated tiers e.g. spot,regional-od,cross-region-od,degrade)
- sla_penalty_usd_per_violation (for hypothetical cost of SLA breach)

Core formulas (expressed so they can be copied into a sheet):
- effective_gpu_cost_per_token_spot = base_gpu_cost_spot_usd_hr / (gpu_throughput_tokens_per_sec * 3600 * batch_effective_multiplier)
- effective_gpu_cost_per_token_od = base_gpu_cost_od_usd_hr / (gpu_throughput_tokens_per_sec * 3600 * batch_effective_multiplier)
- expected_reclaims_per_hour = spot_reclaim_rate_pct_per_hr * spot_mix_pct / 100
- expected_requests_falled_back_pct = 1 - exp(-expected_reclaims_per_hour)   // approximate conversion
- blended_cost_per_token_region = effective_gpu_cost_per_token_spot * (spot_mix_pct/100) + effective_gpu_cost_per_token_od * (1 - spot_mix_pct/100) + fallback_cost_buffer

Notes on fallback_cost_buffer: a tunable value representing temporary higher costs (cross-region transfer, preemption overhead, re-queue). We set initial buffer = $0.001/token for conservative configs.

Quick worked example (single region, numbers approximate):
Inputs:
- base_gpu_cost_spot_usd_hr = 0.50
- base_gpu_cost_od_usd_hr = 1.25
- gpu_throughput_tokens_per_sec = 6000
- batch_effective_multiplier = 2.0
- spot_mix_pct = 60
- spot_reclaim_rate_pct_per_hr = 1.5
- tokens_per_request = 60

Computed:
- effective_gpu_cost_per_token_spot = 0.50 / (6000*3600*2) ≈ 1.157e-8 USD/token  (note: extremely small per-token; convert to microdollars)
- effective_gpu_cost_per_token_od = 1.25 / (6000*3600*2) ≈ 2.892e-8 USD/token
- blended_base = (1.157e-8 * 0.6) + (2.892e-8 * 0.4) ≈ 1.83e-8 USD/token
- tokens_per_request cost ≈ 60 * 1.83e-8 ≈ 1.1e-6 USD/request (GPU only)
- expected_reclaims_per_hour = 1.5 * 60 / 100 = 0.9 (this is scaled for spot_mix; see sensitivity note)
- approximate fallback fraction (by our exp model) = 1 - exp(-0.9) ≈ 0.59  -> indicates this toy paramization is too aggressive (60% of work will need fallback), so either reduce spot_mix or choose more stable regions.

Interpretation: small per-request GPU delta adds up at scale; the dominant decision is how often fallback occurs. The model intentionally separates per-token marginal savings vs expected fallback frequency to show non-linear effects.

Sensitivity slices we recommend creating in the sheet (three tabs):
1) base-scan: vary spot_mix_pct from 0 to 90 in increments of 10, plot cost per 1M tokens and fallback fraction.
2) region-volatility: for each region profile (stable/medium/volatile) sweep reclaim_rate 0.2% -> 5% and spot_mix 0-90.
3) sla-exposure: show expected SLA violations (using latency overheads) for each fallback path and compute expected SLA penalty cost per 1M requests.

Concrete policy recommendations (config knobs):
- Default spot_mix by region profile: stable=70%, medium=50%, volatile=25%.
- Hard cap: never exceed 80% spot_mix in any region for standard tier; enterprise customers default cap 40% unless explicitly approved.
- Fallback ordering: local spot -> local OD/reserved -> regional warm pool (same continent) -> cross-continent OD -> degrade-to-cheaper-model (if enabled) -> reject. Each step increases cost and latency and should be associated with explicit metric tags on traces.
- Autoscaler hint: when fallback fraction > 10% sustained for 15 minutes, recommend incrementing reserved capacity in that region by (fallback_fraction * observed_qps / provision_factor). Provide a formula in the sheet.

Operational runbook snippets (for SRE and support):
- Detection: dashboards show 'fallback_rate' per region/tier. Trigger alert when fallback_rate > 5% sustained for 5m for enterprise customer serving paths, 15m for standard.
- Triage steps: 1) check spot reclaim events (cloud events), 2) check per-GPU utilization and queue growth, 3) if reclaim spikes across many instances, reduce spot_mix for the affected AZ/region and request reserved capacity increase.
- Temporary mitigation: enable cross-region warm pool and restrict routing to enterprise customers to local reserved only until degradation resolved. Notify customer success if ETA > 30m.

Quality / model-regression checks to attach to policy:
- When enabling degrade-to-cheaper-model fallback, run canary evals with a golden prompt set. If model quality drop > 1% by evaluation metric (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/QA F1), disable degrade path for affected customer segments.

Open questions and decision points (for product discussion):
- SLA billing model: do we charge customers for fallback-driven latency penalty or absorb it? (affects opt-in defaults)
- Should customers be allowed to set region_preference_list that refuses cross-region fallback? Default: enterprise can opt-out; standard cannot.
- What is an acceptable operational buffer value for fallback_cost_buffer? Initial suggestion: $0.001/token, but needs calibration to real infra numbers.

Next steps and owners:
- Evan: assemble the spreadsheet tabs (base-scan, region-volatility, sla-exposure) and wire example data. (due: 2025-11-18)
- Priya: add alerting rules and Grafana panel templates for fallback_rate and regional_reclaim_events. (due: 2025-11-15)
- Mariko: run a simulated 48hr experiment using historical reclaim traces to validate recommended default spot_mix values. (due: 2025-11-22)

Appendix: suggested sheet layout (tab names and column headers)
- Tab: base-scan: columns = region, hour, spot_mix_pct, reclaim_rate_pct, base_spot_usd_hr, base_od_usd_hr, throughput_tok_s, batch_mult, effective_cost_spot_per_tok, effective_cost_od_per_tok, blended_cost_per_tok, tokens_per_req, cost_per_req, fallback_frac, cost_with_fallback_per_req.
- Tab: region-volatility: columns = region_profile_label, reclaim_rate_scenario, spot_mix_pct, fallback_frac, cost_1M_tokens, sla_violations_estimated, notes.
- Tab: sla-exposure: columns = customer_tier, latency_slo_ms, fallback_path, added_latency_ms, estimated_sla_violations_per_hour, sla_penalty_usd_hour, blended_cost_usd_hour.

Quick references (links):
- Historical spot reclaim logs: gs://redwood-ops/spot-reclaim-logs/2024-*/
- Existing routing policy code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/tree/main/policies
- Prior optimization PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimizer/pull/397

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Empirically, reclaimed jobs often cause amplification: a single reclaim event can cascade (>1.5x fallback) because requests requeue and hit other saturated GPUs. Need to model cascade risk separately.
- Consider enabling preemptive vacuuming (draining spot for predicted high-QPS windows) to reduce cascade risk.

Feedback requested (quick):
- Are the default spot_mix caps reasonable for sales conversations?
- Is fallback_cost_buffer a useful abstraction or just hiding details?
- Would SRE prefer alerts on reclaim events or on fallback_rate? I lean fallback_rate as it’s more directly tied to customer impact.

End of runbook.
